tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Comparing & Evaluating Dance

questions.question: Q: What is the key difference between comparing and evaluating dance?
questions.correctAnswer: Comparing identifies similarities and differences between works. Evaluating goes further by making a judgement about effectiveness, weighing evidence to reach a supported conclusion about quality or impact.

questions.question: Q: Name three linking words that help structure a comparison answer.
questions.correctAnswer: Similarly, in contrast, whereas. These signal to the examiner that you are making direct comparisons rather than writing about each work separately.

questions.question: Q: What criteria could you use to evaluate the effectiveness of a choreographic work?
questions.correctAnswer: Clarity of intention, audience impact, technical execution, use of choreographic devices, structure, creativity and how well movement communicates meaning are all valid evaluation criteria.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Comparing & Evaluating Dance

questions.question: Q: Why is it important to reference specific moments when comparing two works?
questions.correctAnswer: Specific references demonstrate detailed knowledge and prevent vague generalisations. They allow you to make precise comparisons — for example, 'Both works use canon, but in Work A it creates urgency while in Work B it creates fluidity.'

questions.question: Q: How should you conclude an evaluation answer?
questions.correctAnswer: State a clear judgement that directly answers the question, summarising the key evidence that supports your conclusion. Avoid sitting on the fence — the examiner wants to see you have reached a reasoned decision.
